thread:
oncall-bot: Incident 7895 — p99 latency spike on /v1/generate. Pager sent to @Priya and @Sam. Customers: ~1.1% requests error/timeout. Auto-escalation to platform SLOs enabled.
Priya Patel: taking primary. brief: p99 up from ~450ms -> ~2.3s, errors 502/504. I'll own triage. Sam you stay secondary unless I ask to swap.
Sam Cho: ack. if you need me to step in, ping. do we have warm standby in us-west?
Eli Gomez: I can help infra-side, granting me cluster access please — I'm at a laptop.
Priya Patel: quick checklist: 1) check KV cache hit ratio 2) check model-worker pods 3) check routing fallback to smaller/quantized model 4) inspect request queue lengths. Runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/latency-spike
Priya Patel: commands I'll run:
```
# probe pods
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep model
kubectl top pods -n inference
# scale up
kubectl scale deploy/model-workers --replicas=6 -n inference
```
oncall-bot: Note: scaling has a 30s provisioning lag. Use canary pool if you need immediate throughput.
Sam Cho: if scaling doesn't help, we should enable routing fallback to `quantized-v2` and reduce `max_tokens` for large requests. Route config: https://internal.redwood.com/configs/routing
Priya Patel: started kv-cache probe — hit ratio dropped from 98% -> 45% on 2ndaries. Suspect cache evictions after a config change. OpsBot, any recent deploys touching Redis/kv?
OpsBot: Deploy event recorded: deploy/redis-config v1.4.2 rolled 4m ago by deploy-bot to infra-redis-prod. No immediate errors in deploy logs.
Eli Gomez: eviction policy change could cause higher backend load. Quick mitigation: enable prefix cache warmup and route new sessions to read-only model-serve. See runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback
Priya Patel: enabling cache warmup script now:
```
# warmup (dry run)
python tools/cache_warmup.py --prefix=/v1/generate --concurrency=8
```
Sam Cho: while warmup runs, let's lower client timeouts to reduce retries. Patch consul key: set client.timeout_ms from 5000 -> 2500. Priya can you apply?
Priya Patel: applied patch and rolled 2 nodes (canary). Monitoring metrics.
oncall-bot: Alert update: errors dropping from 1.1% -> 0.6% over last 3m. p99 down to 1.1s.
Priya Patel: trend looks positive. still watching. if p99 stays >1s we'll enact model fallback. Sam, prep traffic shift plan (steps + rollback).
Sam Cho: plan ready: 1) adjust routing policy to prefer `quantized-v2` for payloads < 2k tokens; 2) canary 10% for 5m; 3) if success, ramp to 50% over 15m; 4) monitor quality/regression evals and error rate. Commands and rollback steps in doc.
Eli Gomez: added temporary autoscaler override to prefer spin-up in us-west (more spare GPU headroom). keeping logs on.
Priya Patel: handoff note for next primary (if I need to drop off): state=stabilizing; kv warmup running; autoscaler override applied; routing canary ready; current p99 ~850ms; errors 0.45%. Runbooks used: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/latency-spike , https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/kv-cache-fallback , https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/routing-fallback
Sam Cho: I'll take primary in ~20m if stable, otherwise Priya will close the incident. tagging rotation: @Sam will be primary at 16:40 UTC.
Priya Patel: quick pointer for next oncall: if errors >1% after fallback, rollback routing weights to previous and do a full cache rebuild: `python tools/cache_rebuild.py --force`. Also keep an eye on client retries spiking — that indicates upstream backpressure.
OpsBot: Reminder — incident ticket #7895 updated with mitigation notes and link to burn-rate dashboard: https://internal.redwood.com/dashboards/7895
oncall-bot: Thread closed by Priya Patel at 4112223390 : status=monitoring, action=handoff-scheduled
